modes.name: oled
modes.$description:
OLED, the dark ramp on true black for OLED and AMOLED screens (rule 43). `data-oled` on <html> asks for it and counts only while the dark ramp shows, chosen or from the system, so each value keeps the light ramp's own as its first half. The surfaces move one stone step down and keep their order, so every rule that names a step still lands on the step it meant. The hover keeps its place between the card and surface2, and hover-raised is the step above surface3, as on the dark ramp. The text ramp, the accent and the state hues stay: they were measured on darker grounds than they get here.

The elevation stays dark's shadow. It vanishes on black, and a ring in its place would read as a frame round every card, so a card's near-black is its edge. Over a card the shadow still lifts a bubble or a menu off it. The switch track stays on dark's step rather than following surface3 down, where it would lose its 3:1 on the card. The opaque warning chip stands further from a near-black card than from dark's, and the hairline and the scrim lose nothing on black, so they stay as well. A lit brand tile in a near-black colour, such as GitHub's, would vanish into the card, so --tile-edge rings every lit tile.

modes.name: contrast
modes.$description: The contrast step, for anyone whose system asks for more contrast. It is GlimStone's own and separate from a Windows contrast theme (forced-colors, at the end of this file), which replaces every colour: here the palette stays and only moves. The accent's ink takes a second lightness step in the same ramps, so every preset reads at 8.9 to 9.7:1 as text on white. The sub and muted text each move a step toward the text colour, borders darken to where they read as lines, a card's hairline becomes a ring in the border colour, and the focus ring thickens. The accent fill stays as it is.

also.$description: The same step on request, for an app that offers more contrast as a setting of its own beside the system's: data-contrast="more" on the root.

stone-ground.$description: Ground and surfaces: the stone ramp, OKLCH lightness steps tinted toward the accent's hue. The tint is a share of the accent's chroma that stops at 0.011 on the dark ramp and 0.006 on the light one, so a saturated accent warms or cools the stone without colouring it, and a grey accent leaves it grey. The carbon- names apps read before 5.0.0 stay as aliases of these until 6.0.0, in the legacy block.

carbon-hover.$description: Deprecated, and gone in 6.0.0. Every control hovers to the one --hover (rule 21), so nothing here reads this step. It keeps its value for an app's own rules, and npx glimstone-migrate reports each use rather than rewriting it, since --hover is another colour.

org.glimstone.tailwindNote: Deprecated, and gone in 6.0.0: hover:bg-hover is the one hover (rule 21).

dart.deprecated: Use hover on GlimDerived, the one hover (rule 21). carbonHover goes in 6.0.0.

surface-overlay.$description: Whatever floats over the page, a menu, a list, a bubble, a toast or a window: one stone step above the card on the dark ramps, so it stands off the card it opens over without a frame. On the light ramp it is white, the card's own, and its shadow lifts it.

toggle-off.$description: A switch that is off: 3:1 against the card and against the knob, so the track reads without the knob and the knob without the colour.

toggle-knob.$description: The switch's knob, the same off and on: white on the light ramp, a dark stone on the dark ones, where a white knob would glare.

brand-coffee.$description:
The About card's brand marks at rest, adjusted from the published brand colours. A brand colour is designed against white or its own fill, so on the neutral button ground it fails 3:1 in one theme: #FFDD00 reads 1.14:1 on the light #d1d1d1, and PayPal's navy fails on the dark #525252. Warm brands are deepened for the light theme and dark ones lightened for the dark theme. Contrast: 5.7, 3.3, 3.1 and 7.7 to one on the dark ground, 3.2, 3.2, 8.7 and 11.9 on the light one. Discord's blurple, lightened for the dark theme, reads 3.1 on the dark ground and 3.0 on the light one.

The mail button has no brand colour: it reaches the app's own authors and follows the user's accent. The manual's book takes the yellow of the README's docs button, which is the coffee button's.

brand-android.$description: The App tab's marks that are one flat colour or one gradient, at rest. The dark theme lifts a colour a dark tile would swallow; the light theme keeps the brand's own ("Brand tiles").

stone-text.$description: Text ramp: three steps, the last still legible at 12px.

field-placeholder.$description: A field's placeholder. Muted text falls to 2.4:1 on a sub-card's surface3 field, so a placeholder takes the sub step, the dimmest that reads at 4.5:1 on every field fill.

accent.$description: Activity, and nothing else. Every sibling app opens with this accent, so a fresh install of any of them looks like the same product.

ink-l-light.$description:
The accent used as ink: text or a line-drawn glyph on the page's ground, rather than a fill with computed ink on top, so use this rather than --accent whenever the colour is read. The fill is the same in both themes: Sunflower with computed ink reads well on white, while darkening the fill turns it olive-brown.

The ink is the accent moved in OKLab onto a lightness step, keeping its hue: down to --ink-l-light on the light ramp, up to --ink-l-dark on the dark ones. OKLab's lightness follows the eye, so every hue on one step reads at nearly the same contrast. The light step is set on surface2, the darkest ground accent text stands on in the light theme: the eight presets read at 4.7 to 5.2:1 on it and 5.8 to 6.4:1 on white. A straight line toward black never leaves sRGB; one toward white can by a hair, and the browser clips it. An accent already past the step, a bright one on dark or a deep one on light, is its own ink. applyAccent sets --accent-ink-light or --accent-ink-dark only where a picked colour would still miss 4.5:1 on a ramp's card, which no colour has been found to do (contrast.ts).

accent-ink.$value: var(--accent-ink-light, oklab(from {colour.accent} min(l, {colour.ink-l-light}) calc(a * min(1, {colour.ink-l-light} / l)) calc(b * min(1, {colour.ink-l-light} / l))))

org.glimstone.dark: var(--accent-ink-dark, oklab(from {colour.accent} max(l, {colour.ink-l-dark}) calc(a * min(1, (1 - {colour.ink-l-dark}) / (1 - l))) calc(b * min(1, (1 - {colour.ink-l-dark}) / (1 - l)))))
org.glimstone.tailwindNote: The accent where the colour is read rather than filled (see --accent-ink in tokens.css): text-* and strokes on the page's ground use ink, bg-* keeps text-accent with --accent-contrast on top.

accent-glyph.$description: The same ink for a line-drawn glyph. Rainbow never colours text, so a hued subtree redefines this one and leaves --accent-ink on the single accent.

org.glimstone.tailwindNote: The ink for a line-drawn glyph, which takes a rainbow position where text does not.

status-info-text.$description:
Four state hues, soft and set on one band of lightness per theme, so none of them shouts over the others. A hue's text stands a step further from the ground than its solid, so it reads at 4.5:1 on the hue's own wash. Paused reuses neutral; its label and its resume control carry the difference.

Info is the default accent, so its light text is Sunflower's ink step.

org.glimstone.tailwindNote: A state button: bg-statusOkWash text-statusOk hover:bg-statusOkWashHover, and the same for fail and warn.

status-ok-wash.$description: The fill of a state button: a soft wash of the hue under the hue's own text, a little deeper under the pointer.

status-warn-bg-strong.$description: Opaque, for a chip on a row that already carries a fill the translucent wash would take on.

org.glimstone.tailwindNote: Opaque, for a chip on a row that already has a fill the translucent wash would show through.

status-warn-bg-soft.$description: Quieter, for a paragraph that explains rather than warns, such as the refusal box under "The second way in".

org.glimstone.tailwindNote: The quiet end, for a paragraph that explains rather than warns.

glim-scrim.$description: The ground behind a floating window, light enough that the page still shows where the window came from, and the blur that takes the page's detail away beneath it.

hairline.$description: A surface draws no line of its own: the light engine's edge and the raised step's contact shadow keep a card off the page. The contrast step rings it in the border colour.

focus-ring.$description: The ring is the accent ink, opaque. The ink reads at 4.5:1 on the ramp's card (rule 45), which leaves at least 3:1 on every ground a ring stands on: the page, the rail, a card, a well and a row's hover.

tile-rest.$description: A tile at rest: a quiet wash of the theme's ink, so it still reads as something to press without a grey block, in a well as on a card.

scrollbar-thumb.$description: A scrollbar's thumb, faint on any ground, with no track under it.

selection.$description: Selected text: a wash of the accent under the text's own colour, as strong as it gets while the secondary text on it keeps 4.5:1 for any accent.
